chunks: He said to her, “How long has it been since you gave birth?” She said, “Eighteen [days].” So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, instructed her to perform ghusl, circumambulate the House, and perform salat (prayer), while the blood had not ceased from her, and so she did that.

This also is like the first, because he asked her, “How long has it been since you gave birth?” and she informed him that it had been eighteen days. Had she informed him of less than that, he would also have instructed her to perform ghusl, according to what we have mentioned.

key_terms.الدَّمُ: the blood, referring here to ongoing bleeding
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman with postnatal bleeding regarding ghusl, tawaf, and salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling concerning postnatal bleeding and ritual purity in relation to acts of worship. It indicates that the woman was instructed to perform ghusl and continue tawaf and salat (prayer), showing that ongoing blood in this case did not prevent those rites.
